answer.explanation: top_tto.v muxes the VGA pin mapping on ui_in[7] (`vga_sel`, "pmod sel: high=mole99, low=digilent"). Only when vga_sel=1 does uo_out[7]=hs and uo_out[3]=vs (top_tto.v:82,86), matching the Tiny-VGA-Pmod layout tb.cpp assumes (bit7=hsync, bit3=vsync, comment at tb.cpp:10-11). The harness defaults ui_in=0, so vga_sel=0 selects the Digilent mapping: uo_out[7]=b3 and uo_out[3]=r3 (top_tto.v:79-86) — plain colour bits, not sync. tb.cpp only samples uo_out (line 356), never uio_out, so it never sees the real Digilent-mode hs/vs (which live on uio_out[4]/[5] per the pinout table). What it detects instead is `blu`=bg (the registered blanking flag), which toggles twice per line with a "pulse" equal to the full blanking span (16+96+48=160 clocks) — exactly the reported hsync_pulse_clocks=160 vs the real 96, a smoking gun. The "vsync" signal is really `red`=fg, which toggles every time a paddle/ball/score pixel is drawn, giving the erratic vsync_period_clocks=42 over 376 transitions. Driving ui_in[7]=1 selects mole99 mode, putting genuine hs/vs on uo_out[7]/[3] as the harness expects.
evidence: tb.cpp:10-11 comment: 'bit 7 hsync, bit 3 vsync' (Tiny VGA Pmod layout, matches vga_sel=1 only)
tb.cpp:356 only reads top.uo_out, never uio_out (where real Digilent hs/vs live per pinout table uio[4]/uio[5])
result.json timing: hsync_pulse_clocks=160 == front(16)+sync(96)+back(48) blanking span from vga.v:29-31, not the true 96-clock sync pulse
result.json timing: vsync_transitions=376, vsync_period_clocks=42 — far too fast for a real ~528-line vsync period, consistent with sampling the fg/red pixel-drawing signal instead
answer.video_expectation: A stable 640x480@60Hz Pong-style raster: a dashed centre net, two paddles on the left/right edges controllable via ui_in[0:3], a small bouncing ball, and two score digits at the top — changing/animating as the ball moves and paddles are driven, once the design is put in mole99 pin mode (ui_in[7]=1) so its real hs/vs land where the harness looks for them.
